artifactEvidence.excerpt: Ask for a priority decision instead of silently accepting two incompatible deadlines.

Your manager needs a presentation by tomorrow. You already have a report due then. Before you agree to both, try: “I can finish the presentation tomorrow, but the report would move to Thursday. Which should come first?”

Bring a realistic estimate, including time to check the work. If both deadlines really are fixed, ask what can change: “Could we reduce the report to the essential figures, or could someone take the first draft of the slides?”

Dorie Clark writes about protecting time for chosen priorities and leaving room between commitments. This is a LAiDIES script for making that trade-off visible at work. It will not manufacture extra hours, but it gives your manager a concrete decision to make.

sourceEvidence.excerpt: Building in Margin One of the most overlooked aspects of productivity is margin, creating space between commitments to reduce stress and improve decision-making. I’ve learned to schedule 15-minute buffers between meetings and prioritize direct flights when traveling to avoid unnecessary complications. These small adjustments not only make my days less stressful but also ensure I have the bandwidth to respond effectively when surprises inevitably arise. Guarding Your Time Productivity isn’t just about what you do. It’s also about what you don’t do. Protecting your time requires learning to say no, even when it feels uncomfortable. I’ve developed strategies for triaging requests, such as using scheduling tools to streamline meetings and directing people to resources like articles or webinars when appropriate. These boundaries allow me to focus on the work that aligns with my goals and delivers the most impact. Overcoming Obstacles Procrastination often stems from fear, fear of failure, fear of imperfection, or even fear of success. Identifying the root cause of your hesitation can help you break the cycle. When I notice myself avoiding a task, I pause to ask what’s holding me back and address it directly. This approach helps transform inertia into momentum. Think about your own goals. What are your top two professional and one personal priorities for the next six months? How can you build in margin to handle unexpected challenges? And what forcing functions or boundaries can you implement to stay focused? For more strategies and inspiration, join my email newsletter at https://dorieclark.com/subscribe .
